notes: Account summary: Cirrus is a mid-to-large contact center SaaS provider for retail + telco verticals. Looking to replace in-house LLM routing/assist with platform that guarantees reliability under extreme bursts (seasonal peaks, incident storms).
Primary pain: repeated SLA misses during holiday sale spikes — queues blow out, agent assist timeouts, and backend tools (CRM update calls) rate-limit leading to cascading failures.

Requirements (spoken on discovery call): keep median agent-assist latency <150ms, tail p99 <450ms even under 5x baseline traffic; support 10k concurrent conversational sessions during Black Friday; deterministic fallback to lower-cost model variants under capacity pressure; natice tool-calling to Genesys and internal CRM; audit logs for every call; US-only residency for PII retention.

POC notes: ran a staged load test week of 2026-01-25 with synthetic traffic from their test harness. Observed 30% higher token spend than forecast due to repeated context rehydration — interested in Redwood's prefix/KV cache and warm-pin strategies. Warm-pool suggestion caught interest.

SE feedback (Priya): recommended Dedicated with reserved warm pools + autoscale burst policy + Optimize profile for quantization to reduce per-token cost. Also suggested model routing by priority: high-quality Llama2-70b -> mid-tier quantized 13b -> low-cost 7b for degraded mode.

Security: customer requires SOC2 report, SSO/SAML integration (Okta), KMS integration for key management, and 12-month retention controls configurable per-tenant. Legal flagged indemnity for data residency breaches.

Integration: must support function/tool calling patterns used by their agent desktop to do CRM updates, ticket creation, and automated triage. Need request tracing across Redwood console and their APM (Datadog).
Quote from VP Eng: "We need predictable behavior when the sky falls — not best-effort. If the model degrades, we want graceful fallbacks and clear cost signals."
Pricing/contract: requesting committed monthly capacity with burst pool and explicit per-token overage. Procurement pushing for 12-month term with SLAs on latency and uptime for core assist routes.
Open legal items: addendum for US-only residency, clarify breach notification timeline, acceptable encryption standards in SOW.

Next operational deliverables from Redwood: run joint spike reliability test (two scenarios: 3x sudden incident burst, and 10x seasonal peak for 4h), deliver load test config and scripts, share warm-pool sizing guidance, provide draft SLA language for review.
Internal AE notes: strong exec sponsor (VP Eng / Kara Mitchell). CSM will engage once contract signed. Good upsell path for Optimize and longer-term Private deployment if air-gap requested later.
Risk: competitor (Twilio Flex) offering deeper Genesys plug-ins and existing relationship with their platform team. Need to emphasize better observability and deterministic fallback policies.
